sara: Hi team — customer after prod deploy is seeing an increase in 429s and long tail latencies during short bursts. They report that the failures often come after a flurry of requests and then things recover. Also saw a few 401/billing errors in the same window. Can someone help triage?

prashant: Can you paste the headers + a minimal repro? Thinking this might be a KV-prefetch / prefix-depletion pattern interacting with continuous batching.

sara: Repro steps from customer: small spike (200 concurrent short chat completions) for ~30s, then starts seeing many 429s and 500s. They sent headers and logs (sanitized):

sara: ```
POST /v1/generate 200ms -> 429
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
retry-after: 3
x-kv-cache-hit: false
x-prefetch: false
authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
user-id: 12345

logs:
[2026-03-16T14:02:12Z] request id=abc kv_lookup(prefix=/sessions/u/12345) -> MISS
[2026-03-16T14:02:12Z] batching: queued (batch_id=42) size=48 waiting=120ms
[2026-03-16T14:02:12Z] runtime: allocate kernel -> delay 80ms
[2026-03-16T14:02:13Z] request id=def response=429 quota_exceeded
```

prashant: Looks like their key hit a quota boundary (x-rate-limit-remaining 0) while the KV cache misses meant requests went to full decode paths and batching pooled more tokens — which pushes token usage higher per-window. Combined with retry storms you hit the per-key quota. The 401/billing errors might indicate a fallback or key rotation too.

emily: I checked the billing logs for that customer and saw their primary API key had just expired/rotated and some requests were authenticated with the org fallback key which is on a lower quota plan. That would explain simultaneous quota_exceeded and 401s.

billing-bot: NOTE: org fallbacks have a 10x lower token cap for free-tier fallbacks. Detected ~70% of requests from user 12345 using fallback key between 14:01:58-14:03:10.

sara: oh interesting. So two problems: KV cache warmup/prefix misses causing heavy token usage per burst, and auth fallback reducing quota. Both combine to look like 'perceived throttling'.

prashant: Suggested immediate steps for customer: 1) rotate and standardize on their correct API key, 2) add a short prefetch for their hot prefixes (or enable x-prefetch header) before spikes, 3) throttle client-side retries (exponential backoff + jitter), 4) if bursts are common, consider dedicated capacity or a higher quota plan.

prashant: Quick repro I ran locally: ran 250 concurrent short requests without prefetch -> KV misses + batching grew -> tokens per second spiked -> x-rate-limit-remaining dropped to 0 within 45s. With prefetch (single prefix fetch before ramp) the same burst kept KV hits >95% and no quota hit.

sara: I shared that repro steps with the customer and asked them to confirm key rotation and try a prefetch. Also asked them to send a sample curl/SDK call and their retry strategy.

emily: Billing will reach out to reconcile the fallback key and offer a temp quota increase while customer validates.

infra-bot: Suggestion: we should add a short diagnostic header in support responses so we can quickly see x-kv-cache-hit and x-used-tokens in the future. Filed: INF-7217.

sara: Action items: 
- sara: ask customer to rotate key and run ramp with prefetch
- prashant: share a tiny prefetch snippet and an SDK flag to enable warmup
- emily: coordinate temporary quota bump with billing and report back

prashant: Prefetch snippet we gave them: ```
# python example
client.prefetch_prefix(user_id=12345, prefixes=['/sessions/u/12345'])
# or set header: x-prefetch: true
```

sara: Customer confirmed key rotation and ran a controlled ramp with prefetch enabled. They reported KV hits jumped to ~96% and the 429s disappeared. :tada:

emily: Billing confirmed temporary bump applied. Closing loop with the customer now.

sara: Closing the thread once I get final confirmation from them tomorrow. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
